payload.description: derived from the plan's `bead_id:` frontmatter field

payload.entry: EVIDENCE (preliminary, before the hosted diagnostic run): (1) Hosted signature is identical in every visible Telemetry contention-test job since 2026-10-19 (>=35 runs, never once completed), e.g. job 118110548551/run 39264991134 (2026-10-19, py3.12.15), 128332909537/run 42347892210, 128421280632/run 42377692789 (SHA 0ba9cfc9f1): `contention soak: 1 repeat(s), 26 workers` at start, 17-30 min of silence, then 1-5 `Received SIGTERM - agent was killed`, (run 42377692789) `Recipe test-contention was terminated on line 766 by signal 15` 0.15 s later, then `##[error]The runner has received a shutdown signal`, then 25 `Terminate orphan process ... (python)`. Zero pytest stdout, not even the session header. (2) pytest 9.x terminal reporter flushes piped stdout on every test logstart/logreport, and xdist schedules no test until all workers have collected; so zero output means no test ever reported: every hosted death happened during 26-way worker collection. (3) `Received SIGTERM - agent was killed` is src/sase/axe/runner_signals.py, installed soft=True AT IMPORT by src/sase/axe/run_agent_runner.py:87; xdist workers that imported it during collection print that line and IGNORE SIGTERM, which is why 25 workers survived and were orphan-killed. The SIGTERM was broad (just recipe child died of signal 15 at the same instant, before the runner logged its own shutdown): a whole-job/runner termination, sender unknown. (4) Local (athena, py3.14.7, pytest 9.1.1, xdist 3.8.0, SHA 5692321a2e): one process collecting the default selection (-m "not slow and not visual", visual paths ignored) = 60,493 items, 84.6 s wall, 53.6 s user + 3.2 s sys, max RSS 1036 MB. 26 workers each collect everything: ~25 CPU-min on 2 pinned CPUs and ~26 GB worker RSS vs a 16 GB ubuntu-latest runner. Local 26-worker subset (3 files, 32 tests) already used 4.4 GB worker RSS. Provisional narrowest mechanism: memory exhaustion during 26-way collection on the hosted runner, ended by a broad SIGTERM of unproven origin. Runtime leak excluded for hosted runs (no test ran); disk unmeasured but not implicated during collection. Sender and memory curve still unknown pending the diagnostic run.

PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP: run_agent_runner installs a soft SIGTERM handler at import time - src/sase/axe/run_agent_runner.py:87 calls install_sigterm_handler("agent", soft=True) as a module side effect, so any process that merely imports the module (every pytest worker that collects a test importing it) prints "Received SIGTERM - agent was killed" and ignores SIGTERM afterwards; in Telemetry this left 25 xdist workers alive after the job SIGTERM (runner orphan cleanup had to kill them) and it can mask SIGTERM-based teardown in tests. Move installation into the runner entry point.

EVIDENCE (local full repro): monitor kyhnsmgpcjx9, athena (64 cpus, Python 3.14.7 vs CI 3.12), systemd-run --user scope MemoryMax=15G MemorySwapMax=4G, SASE_CONTENTION_REPEAT=1, 26 workers worksteal pinned to cpus 0-1, full default selection. RESULT: killed during collection at +398s, exit 143 (just recipe terminated by signal 15); no pytest tally, 0 tests started/finished, no in-flight nodes, no 'pytest was killed by' line (just itself died). COLLECTION: 26/26 workers created, controller saw 25 configured at +8s, 0 workers ever finished collecting (first/last collection-finished = none, 0 items) through +386s. MEMORY: worker RSS rose ~linearly ~40 MB/s aggregate (2.1G@15s, 8.0G@106s, 12.1G@214s, 15.8G@323s; ~610 MB/worker at the cap, vs ~1 GB measured for one full single-process collection, so workers were roughly 60% through collection by memory); peak soak RSS 17.07G / PSS 15.94G (workers 16.95G rss / 15.85G pss; controller 34 MB rss / 4 MB pss; parent 23 MB rss), soak swap peak 3.27G, major faults 292,578. Cgroup memory.current hit max (15.00G) at +323s (memory.events max 123 -> 1898 by +386s -> 3290), cgroup swap filled 0.05G@168s -> 3.71G@386s -> 4.00G, then memory.events oom 2 / oom_kill 1 at ~+397s (host vmstat oom_kill +1). Which process the kernel killed is unknown (kernel log not readable by this user). Host was shared and busy: MemAvailable 13.4G at start, min 4.21G; host SwapFree min 33.1G/64G; loadavg 25 -> 78. PSI avg10 peaks: host memory some 52.64/full 44.24, io some 52.65/full 44.05, cpu some <=5.5; cgroup memory some 90.28/full 27.34. DISK: not a factor - scratch (/var/tmp, same fs as workspace) min free 333.8 GiB / 45.84M inodes, /tmp min free 30.8 GiB / 1,041,779 inodes, scratch used 0.8 MB. TERMINATION: signals.jsonl: SIGTERM SI_USER at +398s from pid 7132 uid 1000 = /usr/lib/systemd/systemd --user (chain 7132 -> 1 /sbin/init), outside the soak tree; journal: 'run-p3626556-i7819716.scope: A process of this unit has been killed by the OOM killer' at 12:30:37 (DefaultOOMPolicy=stop) => systemd stopped the whole scope with SIGTERM. The SIGTERM sender is therefore the unit manager reacting to one OOM kill, not a test. SURVIVAL: 17 workers then sent themselves SIGINT via execnet gateway_base._terminate_execution (channel EOF after controller death) 5-28 s later (kills.jsonl, all 'the worker itself', no hazardous kills of soak pgid/ancestors); still, after the 90 s stop timeout systemd SIGKILLed 12 python processes plus 4 processes with comm 'sase-config-tok' (children forked from the sase-config-token-refresh thread, still pre-exec) at 12:32:07; scope 'Failed with result oom-kill', 15min27s CPU, 15G memory peak, 4G swap peak. SAMPLER GAP: once the root died the descendant walk reported '0 soak processes alive' while the journal shows 16 still alive for 90 s. IMPLICATION FOR HOSTED: full-selection collection x26 workers needs well over 16 GB (>=15.8G at ~60% collected); on a hosted runner a global or cgroup OOM kill inside the runner's systemd unit with OOMPolicy=stop would produce exactly the observed broad SIGTERM + 'runner has received a shutdown signal' with no test ever starting - to be confirmed by the hosted sampler (sender chain should be systemd, oom_kill +1). UNKNOWN locally: OOM victim identity; Python 3.12 footprint; final per-worker collection memory under 26-way contention.

PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP: contention sampler loses the soak tree once its root dies — tests/_contention_sampler.py discovers soak processes by walking descendants of root_pid, so after the controller/just root is killed it reported '0 soak processes alive' at the SIGTERM and in the final sample, while the systemd journal shows 16 processes (12 python workers + 4 pre-exec children forked from the sase-config-token-refresh thread) alive for another 90 s until SIGKILL; track membership by process group/session id or the run's cgroup.procs so survivor RSS, ages and exit timing stay visible during shutdown (local repro, monitor kyhnsmgpcjx9).
